screening_decisions.reason: This study analyzes complications from a large cohort of first-trimester abortions but does not describe a randomized controlled trial comparing different surgical methods. It is an observational study of complication rates.

The abstract explicitly states a randomized study was undertaken to compare conventional vacuum aspiration (VA) and manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) for first trimester abortion. This matches the eligibility criteria of an RCT comparing different surgical methods for first trimester abortion.
This study examines trends in mortality and morbidity before and after a legal change. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing surgical methods for first trimester abortion.

Although this is a randomized trial, the intervention compares a prostaglandin suppository vs placebo, with vacuum aspiration as the surgical method in both groups. It does not compare different surgical methods for first trimester abortion.

The abstract states that 420 women were randomly assigned to either D & C or vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion. This is an RCT comparing two different surgical methods (D&C vs vacuum aspiration) for first trimester abortion.

The abstract explicitly describes a randomized trial comparing manual and electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester elective abortion. This is an RCT comparing two different surgical methods (manual vs electric vacuum aspiration) for first trimester abortion.

The abstract states women were randomly assigned to either MVA or EVA for first trimester abortion. This is an RCT comparing two different surgical methods (manual vs electric vacuum aspiration) for first trimester abortion.
The abstract does not mention randomization or a controlled trial. It describes a comparison of two techniques but lacks explicit random assignment, so it does not clearly meet the RCT criterion.

While this is a randomized trial comparing two types of cannulae (metal vs flexible plastic) for vacuum aspiration, it does not compare different surgical methods (e.g., D&C vs vacuum aspiration, manual vs electric). It compares instruments within the same surgical method (vacuum aspiration).

The abstract states a randomized trial was conducted comparing manual vacuum aspirator and electric vacuum curettage for first trimester abortion. This is an RCT comparing two different surgical methods (manual vs electric vacuum aspiration) for first trimester abortion.
